components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
月, appearing twice side by side, originally depicted two people (or two strings of shells) together — giving 朋 its meaning 'friend, companion.'
又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'

example.hanzi: 他是我的老朋友,我们认识二十年了。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de lǎo péngyou, wǒmen rènshi èrshí nián le.
example.english: He's my old friend — we've known each other for twenty years.
example.fact: 老 prefixed onto a word for a person doesn't necessarily describe age — it signals long-standing familiarity instead (老同学, "old classmate"; 老同事, "old colleague"), so even two twenty-year-olds can call each other 老朋友. Separately, dictionaries also record 老朋友 as an established colloquial euphemism for a menstrual period — the same two characters carrying a completely different, informal sense.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
军 (army) — an army being directed
扌 (hand) — the hand giving the command or wave

example.hanzi: 警察在指挥交通。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài zhǐhuī jiāotōng.
example.english: The police officer is directing traffic.
example.fact: 指挥 does double duty as both a verb ("to direct, command") and a noun ("conductor, commander") — the same word covers directing traffic, commanding troops, and conducting an orchestra. 指 contributes "finger, to point" and 挥 contributes "to wave, swing (the hand)," building a fairly literal picture of hand gestures for directing others.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.
士 (soldier) — 壮 describes someone as strong and robust, like a sturdy soldier.
丬 is only distantly related in sound to zhuàng — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.

example.hanzi: 他身体很强壮,每天都锻炼。
example.pinyin: Tā shēntǐ hěn qiángzhuàng, měitiān dōu duànliàn.
example.english: He's physically strong — he exercises every day.
example.fact: 强壮 specifically describes physical robustness of a body, person or animal — unlike 强 alone, which can also describe abstract strength (国力强, "national power is strong"). Pairing 强 with 壮 (built from 士, "soldier") narrows the meaning down to bodily sturdiness.

components.note: 又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
力 (strength) — 劲 names physical strength or energy.

example.hanzi: 你今天看起来不太对劲,还好吗?
example.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān kàn qǐlai bú tài duìjìn, hái hǎo ma?
example.english: You seem a bit off today — are you okay?
example.fact: 对劲 overwhelmingly appears negated as 不对劲 ("something's not right, off") in everyday speech — the bare positive 对劲 is comparatively rare and can sound slightly incomplete on its own, a pattern shared by a handful of Chinese words that live mostly in their negative form.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.
人 (rén) gives the sound — 认 is pronounced rèn, a close variant of the same sound.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 他变化很大,但我还是认出他了。
example.pinyin: Tā biànhuà hěn dà, dàn wǒ háishi rènchū tā le.
example.english: He's changed a lot, but I still recognized him.
example.fact: The 出 after 认 doesn't mean "to exit" here — as a verb complement it marks succeeding at pulling something out of memory or out of a crowd, the same "figure it out" sense of 出 found in 查出 (also in this batch, "to find out") and 想出 ("to think up, to figure out").

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) gives a hint of the sound — 制 is pronounced zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.
卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'

example.hanzi: 警察穿着蓝色的制服。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá chuānzhe lánsè de zhìfú.
example.english: The police officer is wearing a blue uniform.
example.fact: 制服 covers two distinct senses under one written form — the noun "uniform" (school, police, military) and the verb "to subdue, bring under control" — with 制 contributing a sense of regulation and control to both: a regulated garment on one hand, and controlling a person on the other.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坏 relates to something crumbling or deteriorating, like broken soil.
不 (bù) reflects an old phonetic link that has largely faded in the modern pronunciation huài.

example.hanzi: 撒谎是一件坏事。
example.pinyin: Sāhuǎng shì yí jiàn huàishì.
example.english: Lying is a bad thing to do.
example.fact: 坏事 pairs the everyday adjective 坏 ("bad, broken") with 事 ("matter, affair") to name a wrongdoing, mirroring its direct opposite 好事 ("a good deed") — both built from the same simple adjective-plus-"matter" pattern.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 警方终于查出了真相。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhōngyú cháchū le zhēnxiàng.
example.english: The police finally found out the truth.
example.fact: 查 alone just means "to check, look into," but attaching the result-complement 出 ("out") turns it into "to check and succeed in finding out" — a common Chinese pattern where a bare verb needs a complement like 出/到/见 to confirm the action actually succeeded, not just that it was attempted.

components.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.

example.hanzi: 这扇门是自动的。
example.pinyin: Zhè shàn mén shì zìdòng de.
example.english: This door is automatic.
example.fact: 自动 literally builds "self" (自) + "move" (动) — "moving by itself" — the same transparent "self-X" pattern recurs in common words like 自己 ("oneself") and 自然 ("nature," literally "self-so"), a productive prefix worth recognizing across many compounds.

components.note: 氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'
阝 (a mound/enclosure) — relates to 院's meaning 'courtyard, institution,' an enclosed place.
完 (wán) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from yuàn.

example.hanzi: 她要去法院打官司。
example.pinyin: Tā yào qù fǎyuàn dǎ guānsi.
example.english: She's going to court to file a lawsuit.
example.fact: 院 in 法院 doesn't mean "hospital" — its core sense is simply "an enclosed institutional compound" (walled by 阝, the mound/enclosure radical), the same root shared by 医院 ("hospital") and 学院 ("college"), each just a different institution housed within walls.

components.note: 西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
王 here is a variant of 玉 (jade), appearing once on each side of the character.
刂 (knife) — cutting a piece of jade in two, symbolizing a division into groups, gave 班 its meaning 'class, group.'

example.hanzi: 他明年要去西班牙旅游。
example.pinyin: Tā míngnián yào qù Xībānyá lǜyóu.
example.english: He's going to travel to Spain next year.
example.fact: 西班牙 is mostly a phonetic transliteration of "España" — 西 ("west") happens to also fit the country's location relative to China, but the "-班牙" syllables were chosen for their sound rather than their meaning, the same transliteration strategy behind country names like 意大利 (Italy) and 加拿大 (Canada).

components.note: 十 (here a straight vertical line) — 直 pictures something drawn perfectly straight.
目 (eye) — looking directly and steadily with the eye gave 直 its meaning 'straight' or 'direct.'
扌 (hand) — the hand doing the sowing.
番 (a field marked out into plots) — seeds scattered by hand across it, giving 播 its meaning 'to sow, to spread, to broadcast.'

example.hanzi: 这场比赛会在网上直播。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài huì zài wǎngshàng zhíbō.
example.english: This match will be livestreamed online.
example.fact: 直播 literally means "straight, direct" (直) + "broadcast" (播) — broadcasting with no delay or edit — and the word slid seamlessly from television and radio into today's internet livestreaming without needing a new coinage, since the old TV-era term already captured the same "unedited, real-time" idea.

meanings: (fig.) to have nothing further to do (with sb or sth)

components.note: 手 (hand), shown twice, side by side — two hands pressed together in a gesture of respect, giving 拜 its meaning 'to bow, to pay respects.'
手 (hand), shown twice, side by side — two hands pressed together in a gesture of respect, giving 拜 its meaning 'to bow, to pay respects.'

example.hanzi: 我先走了,拜拜!
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiān zǒu le, báibái!
example.english: I'm heading out now, bye-bye!
example.fact: 拜拜 is a phonetic loan from English "bye-bye" — dictionaries list its main pronunciation as báibái (tone 2), which breaks from 拜's ordinary reading bài (as in 拜访, "to pay a visit"). Some sources also record a bāibāi (tone 1) variant, reflecting the word's status as a fairly recent borrowing rather than native vocabulary.

meanings: to shift to an earlier date
to do sth ahead of time

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 我们提前到了机场。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen tíqián dào le jīchǎng.
example.english: We arrived at the airport ahead of schedule.
example.fact: 提前 works as both a verb ("to move something earlier," 会议提前了, "the meeting got moved earlier") and an adverb ("in advance," 提前通知, "notify in advance") without changing form. 提 contributes "to raise, lift" and 前 contributes "before, ahead," as if lifting an event forward in time.

components.note: 示 (an altar) — where offerings to ancestors are made
宀 (a roof) — the home where the family altar is kept
攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) gives a hint of the sound — 教 is pronounced jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.

example.hanzi: 他对不同的宗教很感兴趣。
example.pinyin: Tā duì bùtóng de zōngjiào hěn gǎn xìngqù.
example.english: He's very interested in different religions.
example.fact: 宗 pictures a roof (宀) over an altar (示) — a household's ancestral shrine — while 教 relates to instruction and discipline. 宗教 literally combines "ancestral worship" with "teaching," reflecting how the modern word for "religion" grew out of older vocabulary for lineage ritual and moral instruction.

components.note: 虫 (worm, insect) — 蠢 originally described the wriggling movement of insects.
春 (chūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 蠢, differing only in tone.
贝 (shell/money) — 货 relates to goods that are bought and sold for money
化 (huà) gives a sound distantly related to 货's reading huò, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 别听他的,他就是个蠢货。
example.pinyin: Bié tīng tā de, tā jiùshì gè chǔnhuò.
example.english: Don't listen to him, he's just an idiot.
example.fact: 货 ("goods, merchandise") shows up as a mildly dehumanizing suffix in a small family of insults — 蠢货 ("idiot"), 傻货 ("fool"), 废货 ("useless piece of junk") — literally treating the person being insulted as a defective product, worth noting since 货 alone is a completely neutral word.

components.note: 从 (two people, one following another) — depicts people together.
土 (earth/ground) — two people seated on the ground gave 坐 its meaning 'to sit.'
宀 (a roof) on top represents an enclosed structure.
牛 (cattle) below is the animal kept inside, giving 牢 its meaning 'pen, stable' and later 'prison.'

example.hanzi: 小偷因为偷东西被警察抓去坐牢了。
example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu yīnwèi tōu dōngxi bèi jǐngchá zhuā qù zuòláo le.
example.english: The thief was caught by the police and sent to prison for stealing.
example.fact: 坐牢 is a separable verb-object compound at heart: a time duration can slide directly into the middle of it in speech — 坐三年牢, literally "sit three years prison," meaning "serve three years in prison" — a flexibility English's fused verb "to imprison" doesn't allow. The same separability shows up in 关门 (also in this batch): 关了两次门, "closed the door twice."

meanings: to take care that one does not

components.note: 扌 (hand) — suggests a gesture, a beckoning motion.
召 depicts a call or summons — a hand gesture calling someone over gave 招 its meaning 'to beckon, to recruit.'
口 (mouth) — 呼 describes an action of the mouth, such as calling out or breathing.
乎 (hū) gives the sound — an exact match with 呼.

example.hanzi: 他看到我就跟我打招呼。
example.pinyin: Tā kàndào wǒ jiù gēn wǒ dǎ zhāohu.
example.english: As soon as he saw me, he said hello to me.
example.fact: 招呼 almost always appears inside the fixed collocation 打招呼 ("to greet," literally "to strike a greeting") rather than standing alone as a bare verb — one of a large family of set phrases built around the near-empty light verb 打, alongside 打电话 ("to make a phone call") and 打篮球 ("to play basketball").

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 崩 describes a mountain or structure collapsing.
朋 (péng) gives a sound close to bēng, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.
氵 (water) — 溃 originally described a river bursting its banks.
贵 (guì) gives the sound — a close match for kuì, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,她整个人都崩溃了。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā zhěnggè rén dōu bēngkuì le.
example.english: Hearing this news, she completely fell apart.
example.fact: While 崩溃 can describe a literal physical collapse — a mountain giving way, a bridge, an economy — it's just as often used for a mental or emotional breakdown (心理崩溃, "psychological collapse"), extending the old image of a mountain crumbling (崩, built on 山) or a riverbank bursting (溃, built on 氵) onto inner experience.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 依 relates to a person relying or leaning on something
衣 (yī) gives the sound — 依 is also pronounced yī, an exact match
灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) gives the sound — 然 is also pronounced rán, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 多年过去了,他依然爱着她。
example.pinyin: Duō nián guò le, tā yīrán àizhe tā.
example.english: Many years have passed, and he still loves her.
example.fact: 依然 is a more literary, written-register synonym of the everyday 还是/仍然 ("still") — it turns up far more often in narration, formal writing, and lyrics than in casual conversation, where a native speaker chatting with friends would default to 还是 or plain 还 instead.

components.note: 平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
青 (blue-green, nature) — 静 relates to a calm stillness, like still water or clear skies
争 (zhēng) gives a sound distantly related to 静's reading jìng, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 湖面非常平静,像一面镜子。
example.pinyin: Húmiàn fēicháng píngjìng, xiàng yí miàn jìngzi.
example.english: The lake's surface is very calm, like a mirror.
example.fact: 平静 describes an absence of disturbance — calm water, a calm mood, a calm situation — and is distinct from 安静 ("quiet," about the absence of noise specifically): a room can be 安静 without necessarily being 平静, and vice versa, a distinction English's single word "calm/quiet" often collapses.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 邮局就在银行的右边。
example.pinyin: Yóujú jiù zài yínháng de yòubian.
example.english: The post office is right on the right side of the bank.
example.fact: 右边 mirrors 左边 ("left side") as one of Mandarin's basic spatial pairs, both built the same way from a direction word plus 边 ("side, edge") — 边 itself is a highly productive suffix that turns almost any location word into "the X side" (里边 "inside," 外边 "outside," 前边 "the front side").

components.note: 冂 (an enclosure or doorway) — 内 pictures the space one enters.
人 (person) — a person entering an enclosure gave 内 its meaning 'inside' or 'within.'
衤 (clothes) — 裤 names a piece of clothing, trousers.
库 (kù) gives the sound — an exact match with 裤.

example.hanzi: 他把内裤和衣服分开洗。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ nèikù hé yīfu fēnkāi xǐ.
example.english: He washes his underwear separately from his clothes.
example.fact: 内裤 builds transparently from 内 ("inner, inside") plus 裤 ("trousers, pants") — literally "inner pants" — the same "inner-" prefix pattern behind 内衣 ("underwear" in general, literally "inner clothes") and 内心 ("one's inner heart/feelings").

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

example.hanzi: 他们结婚不久就有了孩子。
example.pinyin: Tāmen jiéhūn bùjiǔ jiù yǒu le háizi.
example.english: They had a child not long after they got married.
example.fact: 不久 almost always anchors to a reference point rather than floating freely the way 快 ("soon") can — 结婚不久 ("not long after marrying"), 不久以前 ("not long ago"), 不久以后 ("before long") — with the anchor coming either just before the phrase or built directly into it.

components.note: 冫 (water/ice) — 冲 relates to liquid, as in pouring or rinsing with water
中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to 冲's reading chōng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
氵 (water) — 浪 names movement on the surface of water, a wave.
良 (liáng) gives a rhyme close to làng, with a different initial and tone.

example.hanzi: 夏天他喜欢去海边冲浪。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān tā xǐhuan qù hǎibiān chōnglàng.
example.english: In summer he likes to go surfing at the beach.
example.fact: 冲浪 literally means "to charge, rush at (冲) a wave (浪)" — a fairly recent coinage for the imported sport — and the same 冲 root now also covers "to rush online" in the internet-era slang 网上冲浪 ("to surf the web"), an extension that echoes English's own reuse of "surf" for browsing.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'
大 (big, a person with arms and legs spread) pictures a person.
镸 (long) pictures a long piece of cloth wrapped around them, giving 套 its meaning 'cover, case.'

example.hanzi: 外面很冷,记得穿外套。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, jìde chuān wàitào.
example.english: It's cold outside, remember to wear a coat.
example.fact: 外套 literally means "outer (外) covering (套)" — 套 alone names any covering that slips over something else (手套, "gloves," literally "hand cover"; 枕套, "pillowcase") — so 外套 simply pictures a coat as the covering worn on the outside, over everything else.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

example.hanzi: 结婚是人生中的一件大事。
example.pinyin: Jiéhūn shì rénshēng zhōng de yí jiàn dàshì.
example.english: Getting married is a major event in life.
example.fact: 大事 sits opposite 小事 ("a trivial matter") on Mandarin's basic big/small scale for how much something matters — the two even combine into the paired saying 大事化小,小事化了 ("turn big problems into small ones, and small ones into nothing"), commonly offered as advice not to escalate a conflict.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吓 relates to a shout or cry, as when someone is frightened.
下 (xià) gives the sound — an exact match with 吓.
土 (earth) — 坏 relates to something crumbling or deteriorating, like broken soil.
不 (bù) reflects an old phonetic link that has largely faded in the modern pronunciation huài.

example.hanzi: 那个声音把孩子吓坏了。
example.pinyin: Nàge shēngyīn bǎ háizi xiàhuài le.
example.english: That sound terrified the child.
example.fact: 坏 as a verb complement after 吓 doesn't mean "broken" here but marks an emotional or physical state pushed to an extreme — the same intensifying use of 坏 shows up in 累坏 ("exhausted, worn out") and 气坏 ("furious to the point of breaking"), a small family of "verb + 坏" compounds for a reaction pushed past its limit.

components.note: 阝 (a mound, related to terrain) — the ground where something happens.
臽 (a pit) — a hole in the ground, together giving 陷 its meaning 'to sink, to fall into a trap.'
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 公司陷入了严重的财务危机。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī xiànrù le yánzhòng de cáiwù wēijī.
example.english: The company sank into a serious financial crisis.
example.fact: 陷入 is almost always followed directly by an undesirable abstract state — 陷入危机 ("sink into crisis"), 陷入困境 ("land in a predicament"), 陷入沉思 ("sink into deep thought") — rarely a literal hole, even though 陷 itself pictures exactly that: a pit (臽) dug into raised terrain (阝).

components.note: 毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).

example.hanzi: 她刚发表了一篇新的论文。
example.pinyin: Tā gāng fābiǎo le yì piān xīn de lùnwén.
example.english: She just published a new academic paper.
example.fact: 发表 covers publishing writing (论文, "papers"; 文章, "articles") and also publicly voicing an opinion (发表意见, "to voice an opinion"). 发 contributes "to release, send out" and 表 contributes "to show, express" — together the word means "to release into view," equally at home with a printed paper or a spoken opinion.

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'

example.hanzi: 父母对孩子的爱不求回报。
example.pinyin: Fùmǔ duì háizi de ài bù qiú huíbào.
example.english: Parents' love for their children doesn't seek anything in return.
example.fact: 回报 carries both a warmly reciprocal sense ("to repay a kindness," 回报社会, "to give back to society") and a sharper sense of retaliation or payback for wrongs, depending entirely on context — the same neutral "return" core (回, "to go back") stretched to cover both gratitude and revenge, where English usually needs different words for the two.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time
讠 (speech) — 讲 relates to speaking, explaining, telling
井 (jǐng) gives a sound close to 讲's reading jiǎng

example.hanzi: 他明天要在大会上演讲。
example.pinyin: Tā míngtiān yào zài dàhuì shàng yǎnjiǎng.
example.english: He is going to give a speech at the conference tomorrow.
example.fact: 演讲 is reserved for a formal, prepared public speech — a lecture, a conference talk, a commencement address — while everyday chatting uses 讲话 or plain 说话 instead; reaching for 演讲 to describe a casual conversation would sound comically over-formal.

components.note: 我 (wǒ) reflects the character's phonetic root, though the sound has diverged over time from the modern reading é.
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.

example.hanzi: 十九世纪的俄国出现了很多伟大的作家。
example.pinyin: Shíjiǔ shìjì de Éguó chūxiàn le hěn duō wěidà de zuòjiā.
example.english: Many great writers emerged from 19th-century Russia.
example.fact: 俄国 is the older, historically-flavored name for Russia, most natural in a historical or literary context like this one; present-day news and official contexts more often use the fuller transliteration 俄罗斯 — both trace their opening syllable to the same sound-match for "Ros-/Rus-."

components.note: 广 (a building/shelter) — 底 relates to the base or bottom, as of a structure
氐 (dǐ) gives the sound — 底 is also pronounced dǐ, an exact match
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 钥匙就在椅子底下。
example.pinyin: Yàoshi jiù zài yǐzi dǐxia.
example.english: The key is right underneath the chair.
example.fact: 底下 names the physical space directly beneath something (椅子底下, "under the chair"), much like its close synonym 下面 — but 底 itself, built from 广 ("a structure") over the phonetic 氐, contributes a sense of "the very bottom or base," giving 底下 a slightly more literal "at the base of" flavor.

components.note: 宀 (a roof) — the shelter of a house.
且 here representing an altar or memorial tablet, together suggesting a fitting, proper ceremony held at home, giving 宜 its meaning 'suitable, fitting.'

example.hanzi: 这条裙子很便宜,才五十块。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi hěn piányi, cái wǔshí kuài.
example.english: This skirt is really cheap, only fifty yuan.
example.fact: 便宜 hides two unrelated readings behind the same two characters: the common, everyday piányi ("cheap, inexpensive") and the rarer, more literary biànyí ("convenient, fitting"). This card corrects an earlier draft that surfaced the rare biànyí reading for this everyday word — the same dictionary-ordering trap that hit 告诉 and 东西 elsewhere in this deck.

components.note: 日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 我们何时才能再见?
example.pinyin: Wǒmen héshí cái néng zàijiàn?
example.english: When will we be able to meet again?
example.fact: 何时 is the literary, written-register counterpart to everyday 什么时候 ("when"). 何 is a classical Chinese question word ("what, which") that survives today mostly in fixed formal or poetic expressions (何时, 为何 "why", 如何 "how"), rarely used alone in casual spoken Mandarin.

meanings: (of a shop etc) to close (for the night or permanently)

components.note: 门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.hanzi: 这家店晚上十点关门。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn wǎnshang shí diǎn guānmén.
example.english: This shop closes at ten at night.
example.fact: 关门 is a separable verb-object compound, like many two-character "verb + object" words in Chinese — a duration or aspect marker can slide between the two halves (关了门, "closed the door [already]"; 关过门, "has closed the door before"), a flexibility that a fused English verb like "to close" doesn't allow.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 经 originally referred to the vertical warp threads in weaving.
工 (gōng) gives a related sound cue for 经 (jīng), reflecting an older, closer pronunciation link between the two.
纟 (thread) — 纪 relates to organizing threads in order, extended to mean 'record, era'
己 (jǐ) gives a sound close to 纪's reading jì
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 这位演员的经纪人正在和电影公司谈判。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi yǎnyuán de jīngjìrén zhèngzài hé diànyǐng gōngsī tánpàn.
example.english: This actor's agent is negotiating with the film company.
example.fact: 经纪人 stacks three characters that each independently live in the "managing affairs" space — 经 ("to manage, to pass through"), 纪 ("to record, put in order"), and 人 ("person") — literally "a person who manages and organizes [transactions]," today covering everything from a sports agent to a real-estate broker.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 停 relates to a person coming to a halt
亭 (tíng) gives the sound — an exact match with 停's reading tíng
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 商场旁边有一个很大的停车场。
example.pinyin: Shāngchǎng pángbiān yǒu yí gè hěn dà de tíngchēchǎng.
example.english: There's a very big parking lot next to the mall.
example.fact: 停车场 is built with total transparency from "to stop" (停) + "vehicle" (车) + "an open plot of ground" (场, the same 场 found in 广场, "public square," and 农场, "farm") — a "vehicle-stopping ground," one of the easiest three-character compounds to decode on sight.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 判 originally related to cutting something apart to distinguish or decide
半 (bàn) gives a sound close to 判's reading pàn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
斤 (an axe) — cutting through something.
米 (grain, in the simplified form; a bundle of thread in the traditional 斷) — the material being cut, giving 断 its meaning 'to break off, cut, sever.'

example.hanzi: 很难判断他说的是不是真的。
example.pinyin: Hěn nán pànduàn tā shuō de shì bu shì zhēn de.
example.english: It's hard to judge whether what he says is true.
example.fact: 判 and 断 are already near-synonyms on their own — 判 ("to judge, to sentence") and 断 ("to decide, to cut off") — and 判断 doubles them into a single verb for weighing evidence and reaching a conclusion, the same synonym-doubling strategy behind compounds like 喜欢 and 应该.

components.note: 长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 孩子的成长需要父母的陪伴。
example.pinyin: Háizi de chéngzhǎng xūyào fùmǔ de péibàn.
example.english: A child's growth requires the companionship of their parents.
example.fact: 成长 differs from the more physical 长大 ("to grow up, get bigger") by leaning toward development and maturation as a process — often used for a person's character, a company's business, or a country's economy "growing," while 长大 stays anchored to literal physical growth, mostly of children.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 试 relates to proposing or trying something out
式 (shì) gives the sound — an exact match with 试's pronunciation shì
马 (horse) — 验 originally related to examining or testing horses, later extended to 'to test, examine, verify'
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 验's reading yàn

example.hanzi: 科学家们正在做一项新的试验。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen zhèngzài zuò yí xiàng xīn de shìyàn.
example.english: The scientists are conducting a new experiment.
example.fact: 试验 (a controlled test or experiment) is a close cousin of 实验 — written with a different first character (试 "to try" vs. 实 "real, actual") but pronounced identically, shìyàn — a near-homophone pair that even native speakers sometimes mix up in casual writing, though usage leans toward 试验 for trials and 实验 for laboratory science.

components.note: 丹 depicts a pellet of red cinnabar mineral, dug from a mine — the source of its meaning 'cinnabar, red, pellet.'

example.hanzi: 丹尼是我们班唯一的外国学生。
example.pinyin: Dānní shì wǒmen bān wéiyī de wàiguó xuésheng.
example.english: Danny is the only foreign student in our class.
example.fact: 丹尼 is a pure sound-based transliteration of the English name "Danny": 丹 (a red mineral pellet) and 尼 (used mainly in transliterations, as in 印度尼西亚, "Indonesia") were chosen for how they sound rather than for any meaning, a common way of rendering foreign personal names in Chinese.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.
林 here depicts eyes shut in sleep, not its usual meaning 'forest.'
夕 (evening, night) — sleeping at night is when dreams occur, giving 梦 its meaning 'dream.'

example.hanzi: 你想跟她结婚?你在做梦!
example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng gēn tā jiéhūn? Nǐ zài zuòmèng!
example.english: You want to marry her? You're dreaming!
example.fact: Beyond literally "to dream" during sleep, 做梦 is just as often used figuratively to dismiss someone's unrealistic hope — 你在做梦 ("you're dreaming, in your dreams") — functioning almost exactly like the English idiom "keep dreaming," a rare case where the figurative sense translates nearly one-to-one.

components.note: 母 (mǔ, 'mother') serves as the phonetic base; the sound has since diverged from měi, so the connection is mostly historical today.
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 我们每年都会去海边旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen měinián dōu huì qù hǎibiān lǚxíng.
example.english: We go on a trip to the beach every year.
example.fact: 每 ("every, each") pairs with almost any time or count word to build a whole family of "every-" expressions — 每天 ("every day"), 每次 ("every time"), 每个人 ("everyone") — and, like the quantifier 所有 ("all"), a 每-phrase is almost always followed later in the sentence by 都 ("without exception") to complete the sense.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 奶 relates to a woman nursing, and to milk.
乃 (nǎi) is an exact match for the sound of 奶.
酉 (originally 'wine jar,' broadened to fermented foods) — 酪 names fermented dairy products like cheese and koumiss.
各 (gè) is the phonetic element from the character's history, but its modern reading no longer resembles 酪's lào — the connection today is historical rather than audible.

example.hanzi: 意大利有很多种奶酪。
example.pinyin: Yìdàlì yǒu hěn duō zhǒng nǎilào.
example.english: Italy has many kinds of cheese.
example.fact: 酪 broadly names fermented dairy foods (built on 酉, originally "wine jar," extended to fermented products) — dairy fermentation is generally thought to have entered Chinese cuisine through nomadic Central Asian influence rather than a native tradition, part of why dairy stays comparatively marginal in classical Chinese cooking.

components.note: 阝 (mound, place) marks a location.
百 (hundred, many) sits beside it — a large, unfamiliar place, giving 陌 its meaning as a raised path between fields, and later, its role in 陌生 ('unfamiliar').
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 妈妈告诉我不要跟陌生人说话。
example.pinyin: Māma gàosu wǒ bú yào gēn mòshēngrén shuōhuà.
example.english: Mom told me not to talk to strangers.
example.fact: 陌生人 is built from 陌生 ("unfamiliar, strange," evoking a raised path 陌 between fields leading to some unknown, distant place) plus 人 ("person"). Its near-opposite, 熟人 ("an acquaintance," built from 熟 "familiar, ripe"), shows the same "quality + person" pattern from the other direction.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water that is deep.
罙 (deep) — combined with water, giving 深 its meaning 'deep.'
刂 (a knife) — 刻 relates to carving with a blade
亥 (hài) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches 刻's modern reading kè

example.hanzi: 这本书给我留下了深刻的印象。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū gěi wǒ liúxià le shēnkè de yìnxiàng.
example.english: This book left a profound impression on me.
example.fact: 深刻 is reserved for abstract depth — a profound idea, a deep impression, incisive understanding — and can't be used for literal physical depth (a deep lake is 很深, never 很深刻); 刻, contributing "to carve, engrave," reinforces the sense of something cut deeply into the mind rather than the ground.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 管 originally referred to a bamboo pipe or tube, later broadening to mean 'to manage' or 'to control.'
官 (guān) gives a hint of the sound — 管 is pronounced guǎn, a connection that has shifted only slightly in tone.

example.hanzi: 这个办法很管用,一试就成功了。
example.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ hěn guǎnyòng, yí shì jiù chénggōng le.
example.english: This method really works — it succeeded on the first try.
example.fact: 管用 is a colloquial, spoken-register word for "effective, does the job" — mostly describing a method, tool, or remedy actually working as intended — sitting alongside the more formal, written-register 有效 ("effective") as its everyday-conversation counterpart.

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 室's reading shì

example.hanzi: 他把旧家具都放在地下室里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ jiù jiājù dōu fàng zài dìxiàshì lǐ.
example.english: He put all the old furniture in the basement.
example.fact: 地下室 builds transparently from "ground" (地) + "under" (下) + "room" (室) — literally "a room underground" — the same "地下" root that gives 地下 alone an extended figurative sense of "underground/clandestine," as in 地下组织 ("an underground organization").
